extracted.intended_audience: general readers, fans, and aspiring/novice comedians
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and examples about stand-up comedic style, content choices, persona/branding, and career diversification drawn from Gabriel Iglesias's biography and public statements. Useful for aspiring comedians shaping material and career strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep material clean and broadly relatable
rubrics_metrics.description: In the beginning, work as clean as you possibly can and stay away from topics that could be controversial or offensive. For example, don't talk about politics, don't talk about religion. Stay away from sports. Talk about things that are relatable to everyone. The more relatability you have, the bigger the fan base you're going to have.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice quoted from a January 2016 interview; presented as a strategy for novice comedians to widen their fan base by avoiding controversial topics and prioritizing universally relatable subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genres and subject-matter to draw from
rubrics_metrics.description: Genres: Observational comedy, surreal humour, self-deprecation, impressions, satire. Subjects: Latin American culture, race relations, obesity, everyday life, pop culture, social awkwardness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists these as Iglesias's typical genres and recurring subjects — they serve as exemplar content domains a comedian might use to craft material that resonates with particular audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop a recognizable persona and recurring bits/catchphrases
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a trademark persona and recurring bits — e.g., Iglesias's catchphrase 'I'm not fat, I'm fluffy' and the 'levels' of fatness bit (Big, Healthy, Husky, Fluffy, DAMN!, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The biography shows how a memorable catchphrase/recurring bit and consistent persona (appearance, signature clothing) can become part of a comedian's brand and help audience recognition and marketing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversify across media and production roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursue stand-up specials, television and film appearances (live-action and voice work), and create/produce shows — examples include producing stand-up specials for Comedy Central and Netflix, hosting 'Stand Up Revolution', creating/producing 'Fluffy's Food Adventures', and acting/voice roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Iglesias's career trajectory illustrates a strategy of expanding beyond live stand-up into TV, film, voice acting, and production roles to increase exposure, revenue streams, and career resilience.
